items.name: 5-Amino-1MQ
items.benefits: Preclinical evidence only: the NNMT inhibitor 5-Amino-1MQ reduced body weight, white adipose tissue mass, adipocyte size, and total plasma cholesterol in diet-induced obese mice. These animal results do not establish weight-loss, metabolic, or anti-aging benefits in humans.

source_statements.section: Who 5-Amino-1MQ Is For and Who Should Avoid It
source_statements.excerpt: 5-Amino-1MQ has no FDA-approved use, so there is no formal eligibility list. The list below reflects how the published rodent studies were set up and what is known about NNMT in human biology.

source_statements.section: Who 5-Amino-1MQ Is For and Who Should Avoid It
source_statements.excerpt: Pregnancy and breastfeeding : not studied. Avoid.

source_statements.section: Who 5-Amino-1MQ Is For and Who Should Avoid It
source_statements.excerpt: Active cancer or recent cancer history : NNMT plays a complex role in cancer biology. In some tumor types, NNMT activity helps the tumor grow; in others, the picture is less clear. Until human safety data exists, anyone with a cancer history should avoid 5-Amino-1MQ outside formal oncology research.

Possible side effects are not well defined because no controlled human safety trial has been published. Informal reports mention sleep trouble, warmth, a faster resting heart rate, stomach upset, and injection-site stinging. Their true frequency and cause are unknown, and long-term risks, drug interactions, and safe-use groups have not been established.
What is known and unknown about 5-Amino-1MQ safety
Sleep trouble, warmth, or a faster resting heart rate
Reported, but not confirmed in a controlled study
Frequency, dose link, and cause are unknown. Other stimulants may add to these effects.
